name: yates_setup
title: Method for adding new models to the yates function

origin.description: A method which yates calls to set up the prediction for a model type. Methods for glm, coxph, and default are part of the survival package. The linear predictor returns NULL.
origin.details: If the predicted value should be the linear predictor, the function should return NULL. Otherwise it should return a prediction function or a list of two elements containing the prediction function and a summary function. The prediction function is passed the linear predictor as a single argument and returns a vector of predicted values.
origin.value: NULL for the linear predictor, or a prediction function.
origin.example:
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(survival))
cfit <- coxph(Surv(time, status) ~ age + sex, data = lung)
gfit <- glm(I(status == 2) ~ age, family = binomial, data = lung)
eta <- c(-1, 0, 1)
value <- c(
  as.character(is.null(yates_setup(cfit))),
  sprintf("%.17g", yates_setup(cfit, predict = "risk")(eta, NULL)),
  sprintf("%.17g", yates_setup(gfit, predict = "response")(eta, NULL))
)
cat(paste(value, collapse = "\n"), "\n", sep = "")

translation.description: Python keeps the three methods as ordinary functions. yates_setup dispatches on the fit's class, as UseMethod does. The coxph predict = "survival" branch builds the default curve from coxsurv_fit and needs the fit's stored x (fit with x = TRUE).
arguments: fit: a fit with a class key or attribute, such as coxph or glm
predict: the type for coxph and glm, matched as R's match.arg
type: the type for the default method
translation.details: A glm fit needs family.linkinv for predict = "response". The coxph survival branch raises NotImplementedError for weights, offsets, or a model with no covariates.
translation.value: None for the linear predictor, or a Python function taking eta and X.
